headline: RBA hikes rates to 18-year high as the US strikes Iran near the Strait of Hormuz — oil spikes and markets feel the heat.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dropped nearly 3% last night after its FY27 Q1 earnings landed. Despite strong Azure cloud growth, investors appeared to sell on concerns about the pace of AI-related capital spending and whether returns will justify the massive investment. A big single-session move, but the long-term cloud + AI story remains intact.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI fell 2.6% today, dragged down by weakness in global tech stocks — particularly Microsoft, which is a major holding. The RBA rate hike also dampened risk appetite on the ASX, hitting growth-oriented ETFs hardest.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two ticked up 1% last night as GTA 6 hype continues to build — the game now has a confirmed November 19 release date. Positive pre-launch momentum is giving the stock a lift.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS edged up 0.8% today in a modest bounce, but the backdrop remains tough. Citi slashed its lithium price forecast by 40% on weaker battery demand — a serious headwind for the long-term outlook.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS dipped slightly today, reflecting last night's mild S&P 500 pullback. The US market was cautious ahead of midterm elections and as oil prices surged on the Iran conflict.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: Basically flat today — a small dip in line with the broader mixed market. The RBA rate hike adds a little pressure to growth assets, but this is noise for a long-term holder.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Barely moved today. Emerging markets are caught between a firmer US dollar and geopolitical uncertainty around the Iran conflict. Nothing structural has changed.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet was basically flat last night, but there's a bigger story brewing — Seeking Alpha analysis flagged 'serious concerns' for Google Search from recent earnings. AI competition is real and worth watching over the coming quarters.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: Dead flat today — essentially unchanged. A well-diversified all-growth ETF that tends to absorb daily noise well. Nothing to act on here.

watch_today.title: RBA hikes rates to 18-year high — pressure on growth assets
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank lifted the cash rate again today — its fifth hike in this cycle — pushing rates to their highest level in 18 years. Governor Bullock said 'some pain now' will prevent worse pain later, and warned inflation will hurt for at least another year. This squeezes household budgets and makes borrowing more expensive, which tends to weigh on growth-oriented shares and ETFs like VDHG and GXAI. Long-term holders should sit tight — rate cycles turn eventually — but expect continued volatility.

watch_today.title: Microsoft (MSFT) — earnings dip, long-term thesis intact
watch_today.detail: MSFT fell 2.83% last night after Q1 FY27 earnings. The concern isn't that the results were bad — Azure cloud is growing strongly — it's that investors are nervous about massive AI capex spending and when it pays off. For a long-term buy-and-hold investor, this is normal post-earnings volatility. The cloud + AI story is one of the strongest in tech. Hold.

watch_today.title: Pilbara Minerals (PLS) — Citi slashes lithium forecast 40%
watch_today.detail: Citi cut its lithium price forecast by 40% citing weaker-than-expected battery demand. This is a structural headwind, not just short-term noise. PLS is already down ~61% from your cost base. The lithium recovery thesis has been repeatedly delayed. This is worth reassessing — but with the stock already so beaten up, selling now locks in the loss. Hold for now, but watch for any further deterioration in the demand outlook.

watch_today.title: GXAI — AI ETF hit by tech weakness and rate hike
watch_today.detail: GXAI dropped 2.57% today, the biggest mover in your ASX portfolio. It's being squeezed from two directions: global AI/tech stocks (especially Microsoft) fell last night, and today's RBA rate hike further dampened appetite for growth ETFs. Down 17.8% overall from your cost base. The long-term AI growth case is still valid — this is a hold. If you have spare cash, a dip like this could be worth topping up over time.

watch_today.title: US strikes Iran near Strait of Hormuz — oil at $98, watch VTS and global markets
watch_today.detail: The US military struck Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz overnight. Oil jumped 1.75% to $98/barrel. The Strait of Hormuz handles about 20% of global oil supply — any escalation could push oil well above $100, adding to inflation globally. This is a macro risk for your US holdings (VTS, MSFT, GOOG) and could influence the RBA's thinking on future rate moves. Keep an eye on this one this week.

watch_today.title: Take-Two (TTWO) — GTA 6 launches November 19, momentum building
watch_today.detail: GTA 6 now has a confirmed release date of November 19 for PS5 and Xbox. This is the biggest game launch in years and a major catalyst for Take-Two's revenue. The stock nudged up 1% last night. Still down 11% from your cost base overall, but the launch is now weeks away. Hold — and the next 2-3 quarterly reports post-launch will be the real test.

world.summary: A big day globally — the US has struck Iran near the Strait of Hormuz as midterm elections loom, oil is spiking, and a major cyber breach has hit Qantas and other airlines.

stories.title: US strikes Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz
stories.why_it_matters: The US military carried out 'defensive strikes' on Iran's Qeshm Island, located in the strategically critical Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply flows. Trump played down the risk of a wider war, but Israel's Netanyahu has reportedly been pushing for more strikes on Iran. Oil jumped to $98/barrel on the news. If the Strait were disrupted, fuel prices worldwide — including at Australian petrol stations — would spike sharply.

stories.title: US Supreme Court blocks Trump's bid to sideline 20,000 California mail ballots
stories.why_it_matters: The US Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration's emergency request to stop California from counting approximately 20,000 disputed mail-in ballots ahead of today's midterm elections. The court ruled unanimously, meaning those votes will be counted. With control of the House and Senate up for grabs, the outcome of today's midterms will shape whether Trump's agenda can be legislated for the rest of his term — and has major implications for US policy on AI regulation, trade, and foreign affairs.

stories.title: US midterm elections 2026 — what's at stake
stories.why_it_matters: Americans are voting today in the 2026 midterm elections, with all 435 House seats and 34 Senate seats on the line. If Democrats retake either chamber, it would create a split government and likely gridlock Trump's legislative agenda. Markets are watching closely — uncertainty around the result could add volatility to US stocks this week, including your VTS, MSFT, and GOOG holdings.

stories.title: Qantas and major airlines hit in cyber breach
stories.why_it_matters: Qantas and a number of other major airlines have been caught up in a significant cyber breach, according to The Australian. No further details on the extent of the breach are available from the article text, but cyber attacks on airlines typically expose passenger data including names, passport details, contact information, and booking history. If you've flown Qantas recently, it's worth monitoring your email for any official communication from the airline.

stories.title: Major fire at Hindustan Petroleum refinery in India — no casualties
stories.why_it_matters: A major fire broke out at the Hindustan Petroleum refinery in Visakhapatnam, India, on Monday. Authorities confirmed no casualties were reported. While the fire appears contained, refinery incidents in India — a major fuel importer — can add short-term pressure to regional oil prices, which are already elevated due to the US-Iran strikes near the Strait of Hormuz.

markets.summary: The ASX held up reasonably well today, gaining 0.3% despite the RBA rate hike. US markets slipped last night — the NASDAQ fell over 1% — on a mix of tech earnings concerns and rising geopolitical tension. Oil is back near $98 on the Iran strikes, and the Aussie dollar dipped slightly.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session despite the RBA rate hike — resources and banks held the index up.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session saw a mild pullback ahead of US midterms and on Iran tension.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech sold off last night, led by Microsoft's post-earnings drop of nearly 3%.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil jumped on US strikes near Iran's Strait of Hormuz — watch for further moves.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold eased slightly — unusual given the geopolitical tension, suggesting some profit-taking.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar slipped a touch — the RBA hike didn't boost it as some expected, likely because markets had already priced it in.

politics.summary: The RBA dominated domestic news today, hiking rates for the fifth time to an 18-year high. There's also political noise around government spending and the budget.

stories.title: RBA hikes interest rates to 18-year high
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised the cash rate today for the fifth time in its current tightening cycle, pushing rates to their highest level in 18 years. Governor Michele Bullock framed it bluntly: 'some pain now' will prevent worse pain later. The RBA warned inflation will remain a problem for at least another year. For everyday Aussies with a mortgage, this means higher repayments again. For investors, higher rates make borrowing more expensive and tend to push down the value of growth assets like shares.

stories.title: Government spending debate — is Labor on a 'splurge'?
stories.why_it_matters: The Coalition is hammering Labor over what it calls an 'out-of-control' spending splurge, with The Australian reporting claims of a $170 billion budget black hole. Labor and independent economists push back, arguing the spending picture is more complicated. The RBA's rate hike today keeps this debate alive — if government spending is contributing to inflation, it makes the RBA's job harder and could mean rates stay higher for longer.

stories.title: EV tax break under pressure as 112,000 drivers blow the budget
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR reports that 112,000 EV buyers have taken advantage of the government's fringe benefits tax exemption for electric vehicles, blowing out the cost of the scheme beyond original estimates. Calls are growing to axe or cap the tax break. For anyone considering an EV purchase for salary packaging purposes, this policy could tighten or disappear — worth keeping an eye on.

stories.title: High Court debates age-based social media ban
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's High Court is hearing a case challenging the government's under-16 social media ban, grappling with thorny questions around what counts as 'lurking' online — i.e., reading without posting. The outcome will determine how broadly the ban applies and how platforms enforce it. A landmark decision either way could reshape how Australians under 16 use apps like Instagram, TikTok, and Reddit.

ai.summary: The big AI story today is a deepening split in the industry between open-source advocates (Meta, Palantir) and closed-model companies (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google). Meanwhile, Google's Gemini 4 Carbon gets a benchmark review, and Argentina is positioning itself as a regulation-free haven for AI data centres.

stories.title: The Great AI Rift: Meta and Palantir vs OpenAI, Anthropic and Google
stories.why_it_matters: A genuine ideological split is forming in the AI industry. On one side, Meta and Palantir are pushing for open-source AI — where anyone can download, modify, and run the models freely. On the other, OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are keeping their most powerful models closed and proprietary, arguing it's safer. This matters because the outcome shapes who controls the most powerful AI tools — governments, big corporations, or anyone with a laptop. It also affects how AI is regulated after today's US midterms.

stories.title: Gemini 4 Carbon benchmark review — close to Claude, better value
stories.why_it_matters: Google's new Gemini 4 Carbon model was put through its paces in benchmarks and came in just behind Anthropic's Claude — but won on value for money. In practical terms, Gemini 4 Carbon is nearly as capable as the current benchmark leader for AI tasks like coding, writing, and reasoning, but costs developers less to use via the API. Good news for Google's competitive position in the AI race, which matters for your GOOG holding.

stories.title: What AI regulation to expect after the US midterms
stories.why_it_matters: Goldman Sachs has weighed in on what today's US midterm results mean for AI regulation. A Republican-held Congress is expected to favour lighter-touch, industry-friendly AI rules. A Democratic shift could bring stricter oversight closer to the EU model. The outcome directly affects companies like Google, Microsoft, and OpenAI — all of which are heavily exposed to US regulatory decisions on how AI can be built and deployed.

stories.title: Argentina positions itself as a regulation-free AI data centre haven
stories.why_it_matters: Argentina is actively courting AI data centre operators with a combination of zero regulation and generous tax breaks — positioning itself as the 'wild west' for AI infrastructure. Tech giants are always looking for cheap, fast places to build out computing power. For context, AI data centres consume enormous amounts of electricity and need massive investment; countries that attract them get jobs and economic activity, while countries that over-regulate risk missing out entirely.

sport.summary: The Roosters are NRL premiers after a thrilling one-point Grand Final win over the Knights. NRL club brand values are booming, GTA 6 has a firm release date that's exciting Take-Two investors, and there's transfer and coaching news worth knowing.

stories.title: Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over Knights
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters claimed the 2026 NRL premiership in a heart-stopping Grand Final at Accor Stadium, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18. One point in it at the final whistle — it doesn't get much closer. A stunning match to cap the season.

stories.title: NRL and AFL club brand values hit combined $2.9 billion
stories.why_it_matters: The Brand Finance 2026 report valued AFL and NRL clubs at a combined $2.9 billion, with Collingwood overtaking NRL powerhouses to top the list. This reflects the surging commercial appeal of Australian football codes — strong sponsorship, broadcast deals, and fan engagement are driving club valuations higher every year.

stories.title: Benji Marshall's coaching shake-up — new faces at Wests Tigers
stories.why_it_matters: Benji Marshall has made changes to his coaching staff at the Wests Tigers ahead of the 2027 season. There's also a touching tribute to former NRL player Liam Arrow from an English Premier League club, highlighting the reach of NRL culture internationally. The Tigers are rebuilding — new faces in the coaching box signal Marshall is trying to shake things up after a tough year.

stories.title: GTA 6 confirmed for November 19 — PS5 and Xbox release details locked in
stories.why_it_matters: Grand Theft Auto 6 officially launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox. Pre-loading details are now confirmed. This is the most anticipated game release in years and a massive revenue event for Take-Two Interactive (TTWO), which you hold. Strong early sales could be a significant catalyst for the stock over the next 1-2 quarters.
